title: Enterprise Onboarding — Health Checks, QBRs, Escalation & Integration Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Purpose:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s recommended operational process for enterprise customer onboarding, integration handoffs, known-issues triage and workarounds, escalation paths, and recurring health-check / QBR cadence. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and on-call SREs who own customer health and SLAs.

Scope:
- Applies to all paid enterprise and dedicated/private deployment customers.
- Covers the first 90 days of onboarding plus ongoing quarterly engagement (QBRs) and reactive escalation for Sev1/Sev2 incidents.

Summary / Key Goals:
- Deliver a repeatable onboarding experience that reduces time-to-value to <= 14 days for standard integrations.
- Maintain onboarding NPS >= 70 across enterprise accounts.
- Ensure 95% of production escalations are routed and acknowledged within target windows described below.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Customer Success (CSM): project management, QBR ownership, health reviews, renewals.
- Solutions Engineering (SE): integration runbook, API configuration, performance tuning, initial model selection advice.
- Support Engineering (L2): incident triage, root-cause analysis, workaround publications.
- Eng SRE / Runtime Team: capacity validation, SLA verification, hotfixes for production impacting runtime bugs.
- Customer Technical Contact (CTC): primary technical liaison on the customer side.

Onboarding Phases & Checklist (high-level):
1) Discovery (Day 0–3)
   - Deliverables: intake form, success metrics, dedicated Slack channel or PagerDuty integration details.
   - Actions: confirm data residency, compliance controls (KMS/HSM), required throughput and latency targets.
2) Technical Kickoff (Day 3–7)
   - Deliverables: integration runbook, sample API keys, test account, and initial model recommendation.
   - Actions: validate network connectivity (if Private/VPC), exchange certs/whitelists, confirm endpoints.
3) Integration & Validation (Day 7–14)
   - Deliverables: integration verification checklist, performance baselines, security attestation.
   - Actions: run sample traffic, verify tokenization/encoding compatibility, measure p95 latency, embedding similarity sanity checks.
4) Hardening & Rollout (Day 14–30)
   - Deliverables: rollout plan, rollback steps, canary schedule, autoscaling policy.
   - Actions: enable prefix caching if applicable, set batching/quantization profiles, finalize monitoring dashboards.
5) Ongoing Ops (Post Day 30)
   - Deliverables: QBR template, health dashboard subscriptions, runbook handoff.
   - Actions: schedule QBR cadence (quarterly), enable alerting to SRE/team channels.

Integration Guide (SE checklist & sample commands):
- Supported integration methods: REST API (hosted), Private VPC peering (private), gRPC (dedicated private link).
- Sample API health check (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TEST_KEY>' -d '{"check":"runtime"}'

- Required customer configuration items table:
  | Item | Why | Owner | Example/Value |
  |------|-----|-------|---------------|
  | API Key | Auth | CTC | sk_test_XXXX |
  | IP CIDR / Peering | Network | Customer NetOps | 10.240.0.0/16 |
  | KMS Key ARN | Encryption | Security | arn:aws:kms:... |
  | Expected QPS | Capacity planning | SE/CSM | 100 QPS peak |

Known Issues & Workarounds (L2 knowledge):
- Symptom: Increased p95 latency during long-context requests > 8k tokens.
  - Root-cause: runtime kernel fallback to unoptimized attention path for mixed precision models.
  - Workaround: reduce batch_size to 1 for long-context endpoints; enable per-request max_new_tokens limit; recommend model variant quantized for long context.
- Symptom: Embedding drift vs. baseline after model update.
  - Root-cause: model version change without evaluation on customer prompt set.
  - Workaround: roll back to pinned model version; run evaluation harness (see: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness).
- Symptom: Private deployment TLS handshake failures after cert rotation.
  - Root-cause: cert chain mismatch on customer side.
  - Workaround: validate intermediate CA on client; provide diagnostic curl with --verbose; coordinate cert chain push windows.

Escalation Playbook (pagers & SLA targets):
- Severity definitions:
  - Sev1 (P0): Production outage — inference endpoints unreachable or > 90% error rate for customer traffic.
  - Sev2 (P1): Severe degradation — 50–90% error rate or p95 latency > 3x target for > 15 minutes.
  - Sev3 (P2): Functional impact with workaround (degraded quality or intermittent failures).

- Escalation steps (ordered):
  1. Triage by Support (L1): confirm scope, collect logs, request session replay token from CTC. (target: 15 min ack)
  2. L2 Support: reproduce, attach recent request IDs, check model version routing, metrics (error rate, token throughput). (target: 30 min ack)
  3. SE or Runtime Eng (if capacity or regression suspected): change routing policy, increase capacity, or revert model rollout. (target: 1 hour ack)
  4. SRE / Incident Commander: engage for cross-customer outages or infra events (target: 30 min).
  5. Executive & Customer Comms: CSM prepares status updates every 30 minutes for Sev1 until resolved.

- Pager routing & contact matrix:
  - Initial page: support@redwood.ai + on-call L2 (PagerDuty)
  - If unresolved 30m: escalate to Eng SRE (pager)
  - If unresolved 60m or customer requests: loop in SE and CSM for mitigation steps

Support Process & SLAs:
- Standard response targets (enterprise customers):
  - Acknowledgement: Sev1 within 15 minutes, Sev2 within 30 minutes, Sev3 within 4 hours.
  - Initial mitigation plan: Sev1 within 30 minutes, Sev2 within 2 hours.
  - Resolution or rollback target: Sev1 within 4 hours (business hours), Sev2 within 24 hours.
- Communication templates: include incident summary, impact, timeline, mitigation steps, and ETA. Maintain status at status.redwood.ai for cross-team visibility.

Health Checks & QBR Materials (CSM playbook):
- Recommended automated health checks (daily):
  - Token throughput vs committed capacity (24h rolling).
  - Error rate (5xx/4xx) per route (target < 0.5% rolling).
  - Latency: p50/p95/p99 per route (p95 target based on customer SLA).
  - Model drift: comparison of output metrics against baseline prompt set (monthly).

- QBR agenda template (30–60 minutes):
  1. Welcome & objectives (5m)
  2. Usage review (tokens, routes, cost by model) (10m)
  3. Performance & reliability (SLOs, incidents since last QBR) (10m)
  4. Model quality & evals (prompt set regressions, false positives) (10m)
  5. Roadmap & recommendations (optimizations, quantization, batching) (10m)
  6. Action items & next steps (5m)

- QBR deliverables (to be shared after meeting):
  - Executive summary (1 page)
  - Action item tracker with owners and due dates (Jira/Asana links)
  - Updated performance dashboards and historical graphs (last 90 days)

Operational Runbooks & Templates (links and quick references):
- Integration runbook template: steps for generating test traffic, validating KV cache priming, and setting streaming vs non-streaming modes.
- Incident summary template: incident id, timeline, root cause, corrective actions, postmortem owner.
- Rollback checklist: confirm pinned version, health endpoints, customer notified, re-run smoke tests.

Operational thresholds and SLOs (recommended defaults):
- Availability: 99.9% monthly for enterprise endpoints (SLA dependent).
- Error rate: <= 0.5% (5xx) rolling 24h.
- Latency: p95 <= 350ms for short-form generation workloads; p95 <= 1.5s for moderated long-form workloads (policy adjustable).

Review cadence & ownership:
- Playbook owner: Head of Customer Success (Aisha Patel).
- Reviewers: SE lead and Runtime product manager (quarterly review).
- Playbook review frequency: every 6 months or after any Sev1 that impacts >5 customers.

Appendix: Useful diagnostic commands and dashboards
- Logs: support-tool fetch-logs --customer-id <CUST> --since 60m --levels error,warning
- Metrics: Grafana dashboard links (embed): /dashboards/customer/<CUST>/overview
- Evaluation harness: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness
